evidence.intree_statement: Class Functor {C : Category} {D : Category} := { fobj : C → D; fmap {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : fobj x ~> fobj y; fmap_respects : ∀ x y, Proper (respectful equiv equiv) (@fmap x y); fmap_id {x : C} : fmap (@id C x) ≈ id; fmap_comp {x y z : C} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g }

statement_record.book: A functor T : C -> B is a morphism of categories: an object function c |-> Tc and an arrow function f : c -> c' |-> Tf : Tc -> Tc' with T(1_c) = 1_{Tc} and T(g.f) = Tg . Tf; equivalently an arrows-only description (a function on arrows preserving identities and composites).
statement_record.intree: Class Functor := { fobj : C → D; fmap {x y} (f : x ~> y) : fobj x ~> fobj y; fmap_respects; fmap_id : fmap id ≈ id; fmap_comp : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g } (Theory/Functor.v:96-108).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — faithful setoid rephrasing (laws in ≈ on hom-setoids, plus the extra obligation fmap_respects that is invisible under strict equality). The book's secondary arrows-only reformulation is not separately formalized, but the book itself presents it as merely an equivalent phrasing.
